title: Light-sheet Fluorescence Microscopy to Capture 4-Dimensional Images of the Effects of Modulating Shear Stress on the Developing Zebrafish Heart
protocol: Obtain Human Nrg1 cDNA from a donor plasmid.
Amplify Human Nrg1 cDNA for trabeculation rescue.
Take out PCR mastermix from -20 °C storage.
Retrieve primers from -20 °C storage.
Obtain a PCR plate stored at room temperature.
Get a 20 μL pipette stored at room temperature.
Prepare the mastermix for each primer set in triplicate using a 20 μL pipette.
Use 37.5 μL of mastermix, 3 μL of DNA-free water, and 4.5 μL of primer for one set of triplicates.
Dilute working solution Human Nrg1 cDNA (20 ng/μg concentration) in the primer strip with DNA-free water to a total volume of 10 μL per well per sample.
Mix each diluted solution by pipetting up and down.
Use one pipette tip for only one sample to prevent cross-contamination.
Aliquot Nrg1 cDNA using a 10 μL multi-channel pipette into desired wells in the PCR plate.
Add 14.5 μL of mastermix to the cDNA in each well.
Apply a sticky cover to seal the PCR plate wells.
Place the sealed PCR plate into the PCR machine.
Start the PCR machine and ensure appropriate temperatures are reached for enzymes and primers used.
Clone Nrg1 cDNA into plasmid pCS2+ at BamHI and EcoRI sites using excess enzymes BamHI and EcoRI.
Mix Nrg1 cDNA with donor plasmid pCS2+, master mix solution, and primers in a total volume of 50 μL.
Place the mixture in a PCR machine and set parameters to 98 °C for 10 s, 55 °C for 7.5 s, and 72 °C for 5 s/kb.
Purify the PCR product using a purification kit following manufacturer's instructions.
Elute the purified PCR product into 50 μL of elution buffer.
Digest the purified PCR product with BamHI in a 200 μL reaction volume at 37 °C for 2 h.
Digest pCS2+ plasmid with EcoRI separately in a 200 μL reaction volume at 37 °C for 2 h.
Purify each digestion and elute the BamHI-digested PCR product in 20 μL of Tris-HCl (pH 8.5).
Elute the EcoRI-digested pCS2+ plasmid in 100 μL of Tris-HCl (pH 8.5).
Ligate Nrg1 cDNA and digested pCS2+ plasmid in a 25 μL reaction with ligase catalyst at 16 °C overnight.
Transform 2 μL of ligation solution into E. coli bacteria cells suitable for cloning.
Confirm transformation by screening Nrg1 cDNA clones using PCR.
Add random chosen clones to a solution containing specific primers, polymerase, and dNTPs.
Pick 8 colonies from the transformation for screening pCS2+-Nrg1 clones using PCR primers.
Culture one clone with Nrg1 cDNA in LB media (100 μL of E. coli bacteria with pCS2+-Nrg1 plasmid into 100 mL) by shaking at 37 °C.
Transfect purified pCS2+-Nrg1 plasmid into HEK-293 cells in a 6-well plate using a commercial transfection reagent according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Lysate the cells 24 h after transfection using lysis buffer and run through an SDS-PAGE gel, transfer to a gel membrane, and then stain with anti-Nrg1 antibody for Western Blot verification.
Take 5 μL of the pCS2+-Nrg1 DNA from the isolated culture, digest it with NotI in a 200 μL reaction at 37 °C for 2 h to linearize the plasmid.
Purify the linearized plasmid using a commercial kit and elute it in 20 μL of Tris-HCl (pH 8.5).
Conduct in vitro transcription with a commercial RNA isolation kit in a 20 μL reaction using 5 μL of the linearized plasmid following the manufacturer's instructions.
Add the in vitro transcribed Nrg1 to 350 μL of RNA lysis buffer and then purify with an RNA isolation kit.
Elute the RNA into 60 μL of Tris-HCl (pH 8.5).
Measure the RNA concentration.
Store the RNA at -80 °C for future use.
Clone cDNA into the pCS2+ plasmid at EcoRI and XhoI sites.
Design MO injections using an online tool against the ATG sequence of gata1a4 and tnnt2a5.
Add gata1a MO to nuclease-free water to make a final concentration of 8 ng/nL.
Add tnnt2a MO to nuclease-free water to make a final concentration of 4 ng/nL.
Inject 1 nL of the 8 ng/nL gata1a MO and 1 nL of the 4 ng/nL tnnt2a MO into separate zebrafish embryos at the 1- to 4-cell stage.
Prepare EPO mRNA with a final concentration of 20 pg/nL.
Inject 1 nL of 20 pg/nL EPO mRNA into zebrafish embryos at the 1- to 4-cell stage.
Dilute the 10 mg/mL AG1478 in 1% DMSO in E3 medium to a final concentration of 5 μM at 30 hpf in a 15 mL tube.
Treat each fish with 1% DMSO only as a control.
Add N-[N-(3,5-Difluorophenactyl)-L-Alanyl]-S-Phenylglycine t-butyl ester (DAPT) in 1% DMSO (100 μM) to E3 medium in a 15 mL tube to inhibit Notch signaling at 40 hpf.
Treat with only 1% DMSO as a control.
Create a 1% (w/v) agarose gel by adding 1 g of agarose to 100 mL and heating until all agarose is dissolved.
Load a small plastic tube with the embryo and agarose using a 20 μL pipette and secure it on the stage.
Open the image viewing software and click Live to see the live view of the sample.
Adjust the objective using the knob so that the sample is in focus.
Move the stage so that the live view of the sample shows the top of the embryo.
Take images 500 times for 5 s at 10X magnification using the microscope's software.
Move the stage using the motor to a new layer (1 μm in the z-axis).
Repeat the imaging procedure.
Repeat above steps until entire heart is fully imaged.
Disregard the first and last cardiac cycle images for data integrity.
Match images taken at the same time point in different periods of the cardiac cycle.

Calculate the period using the provided equation with D as the cost function, Im as captured image, τ' as capture time, zk as z-direction index, xm as pixel index vector, and T' as periodic hypothesis.

Find the relative shift between two images at similar stages using a cost function Qk',k for possible spatial neighborhood R within total capture time L, x as pixel index, zk and zk' as first and second z-direction slices, t as time, and s as relative shift hypothesis.
Convert the relative shift to an absolute shift with respect to the first image.
Solve the linear equation using a pseudo-inverse approach to find the absolute relation for aligning subsequent sections of images.
Process final 4-D images using commercial image processing software.
Select all the images to be stacked into 3-D.
Click Load after entering the voxel size of 0.65 x 0.65 x 1.
Click the Multi-Planar View box to visualize the 3-D image.
Right-click the blue slice_1.tiff box and select Display, then Volren.
Click Edit > Select Options > Select Edit Colormap.
Adjust the color using the boxes outlined in red and click OK.
Convert 3-D to 4-D by clicking "File > Open Time Series Data".
Select the 3-D tiffs that were just made and click Load.
Enter the same voxel size as before.
Right-click the blue slice_1.tiff box and select Display, then Volren.
Click Edit > Select Options > Select Edit Colormap.
Adjust the color using the boxes and click OK.
Right-click Time Series Control and click Movie maker.
Press the Play button to watch the movie.
Add a file name, frame size, frame rate, quality equal to 1, type Monoscopic and click Apply.
Export the video.
Open the video in an appropriate software.
Sacrifice zebrafish by subjecting them to an overdose of tricaine methylate.
Excise zebrafish hearts using a previously described protocol.
Isolate total RNA from zebrafish hearts.
Synthesize cDNA using the cDNA synthesis kit following the manufacturer's instructions.
Design PCR primers for Notch ligands Jag1, Jag2, Dll4, receptor Notch1b, and signaling related genes Nrg1 and ErbB2.
Add the designed primers, isolated mRNA, and commercial mastermix to the PCR plate.
Run qRT-PCR at appropriate temperatures and times according to the enzymes used.
Normalize the results to zebrafish α-actin.
Culture HAEC cells with HAEC culture media.
Warm up EC media/DMEM 10% FBS in a water bath for 20 min.
Retrieve HAEC cells from liquid nitrogen tank and place the vial into the water bath until melted.
Centrifuge the cell solution at 53 x g for 3 min.
Aspirate the solution off and add enough media for a total volume of 10 mL.
Add the cell solution to a sterile T75 flask, cap the flask, and distribute cells evenly on the bottom of the plate.
Incubate the flask at 37 °C, 5% CO2, until cells are 80% confluent.
Change the media every 2-3 days once cells reach 80% confluence.
Expose fully confluent HAEC cells to laminar flow and pulsatile flow of 23 x 10^-5 N at a rate of 1 Hz for 24 hours.
Attach tubing to the flask using a commercial pump.
Set parameters as mentioned above in step 4.1.131,32,33.
Add GI254023X to 50 mL of HAEC medium at a final concentration of 5 μM for 30 min.
Conduct laminar flow or pulsatile flow experiments with the pre-mixed GI254023X.
Quantify Notch ligands (Jag1, Jag2, and Dll4) using qRT-PCR.
Quantify Notch target genes (hairy and enhancer of split [Hes]) using qRT-PCR.
Inject 1 nL of the prepared Nrg1 mRNA at a concentration of 5 pg/nL into the 1- to 4-cell stage with gata1a MO.
Inject 1 nL of the Nrg1 mRNA into wea mutant in a similar way.
Double the concentration of Nrg1 mRNA (10 pg/nL) and inject 1 nL into zebrafish.
Inject 1 nL of the 20 pg/nL EPO mRNA into zebrafish embryos at the 1- to 4-cell stage.
Inject 1 nL of the 50 μM Isoproterenol into the E3 medium for 24 h while culturing zebrafish.
Perform 4-D LSFM imaging for each group at 50, 75, and 100 hpf.
Divide each image into sections with 600 nodes.
Measure the change in ventricular diameter during diastole and systole.
Load 3-D ventricular images at intervals of every 0.1 s using visualization software.
Measure the volume from the loaded images.
Plot the volume change over time for each experimental group at 75 hpf.
Plot the volume change over time for each experimental group at 100 hpf.
